title: Architecture
text: Rn1_statistics, GOF_model_info_extractor, GOF_model_simulator, GOF_sim_wild_rademacher GOF_model_trainer follow strategy pattern GOF_model_resample follow template pattern. Note object-oriented concepts realized via R6-package R6 actually real interface-functionality abstract classes.

title: New-Models
text: Assume model Y=m(β⊤X)+ϵ Y = m(\beta^\top X) + \epsilon without knowledge ϵ\epsilon. try estimate β\beta using least square estimate using GOF-package check fitted model. First generate data set  Lets short excursion point plot gives impression following simple model might apply: However, goodness--fit-test rejects model Note simple case standard diagnostic plots also reveal model sufficient. Now fit model using least square estimator: order create goodnes--fit-test using GOF_model_test implement three interfaces. first interface requires implement three functions yhat, y_minus_yhat beta_x_covariates, predictions dependent variable (also called target-variable), residuals scale dependent variable inner product estimated parameters independent variables (also called covariates features). However, object returned minpack.lm::nlsLM contain original data set data set necessary calculate inner product. Hence, make list contains model fit data used fit model. Now can implement interface Implementing yhat y_minus_yhat straight forward using function already offered R beta_x_covariates needs special attention. reason minpack.lm::nlsLM can also fit general models type m(β,X)m(\beta, X). Hence, now built--function extract objects like β⊤X\beta^\top X. Lets look first data points: Now able predict yy: calculate difference yy prediction: based estimated coefficient can calculate inner product xx: Since make assumption distribution ϵ\epsilon use parametric resampling scheme. However, can wild bootstrap uses predictions residuals. class GOF_sim_wild_rademacher implements wild bootstrap needs info extractor obtain preditions residuals: class generates many observations (according fitted model) contained data set used fit model. looking first original data points: Now lets look new yys generated according fitted model, .e. following negative binomial distribution subject independent variables: Note resampled yy’s sometimes equal observed yy. reason wild bootstrap performs ‘predictions +/- residual’ sign drawn random. Finally, need implement interface GOF_model_trainer requires function refit able update model object refitting new data set. R already provides necessary function, .e. stats::update. However combined fitted model data set list need take account: implementation basically equals implementation GOF_lm/glm/_trainer. difference store data fit nlsLM() doesn’t us. course, fitting model original data set results fitted model. defined classes can now easily generate new data set refit model new data set. Now ingredients available applying Goodness--Fit test:
code: library(bootGOF) set.seed(1) X = runif(n = 200, min = 6, max = 14) d = data.frame(x = X, y = sin(0.5 * X) + rnorm(200, sd = 0.2)) plot(y~x, data = d) wrong_model = lm(y ~ I(x^2), data = d) mt <- GOF_model(   data = d,   model = wrong_model,   simulator_type = "parametric",   nmb_boot_samples = 100,   y_name = "y",   Rn1_statistic = Rn1_KS$new()) mt$get_pvalue() #> [1] 0 library(minpack.lm) fit <- minpack.lm::nlsLM(y ~ sin(a * x),   data = d,   start = c(a = 0.5),   control = nls.control(maxiter = 500)) fit #> Nonlinear regression model #>   model: y ~ sin(a * x) #>    data: d #>      a  #> 0.4993  #>  residual sum-of-squares: 7.873 #>  #> Number of iterations to convergence: 3  #> Achieved convergence tolerance: 1.49e-08 fit_and_data <- list(fit = fit, data = d) library(R6) my_nls_info_extractor <- R6::R6Class(   classname = "my_nls_info_extractor",   inherit = GOF_model_info_extractor,   public = list(     yhat = function(model) {       predict(object = model$fit)     },     y_minus_yhat = function(model) {       residuals(object = model$fit)     },     beta_x_covariates = function(model) {       a_hat <- coef(object = model$fit)       x <- model$data$x       ret <- a_hat * x       return(ret)     }   )) my_info_extractor <- my_nls_info_extractor$new() head(d) #>           x          y #> 1  8.124069 -0.9199426 #> 2  8.976991 -0.9666172 #> 3 10.582827 -1.0191812 #> 4 13.265662  0.3741709 #> 5  7.613455 -0.7480823 #> 6 13.187117  0.6588717 head(my_info_extractor$yhat(model = fit_and_data)) #> [1] -0.7926252 -0.9737135 -0.8407826  0.3343611 -0.6132205  0.2971500 head(my_info_extractor$y_minus_yhat(model = fit_and_data)) #> [1] -0.127317499  0.007096259 -0.178398577  0.039809752 -0.134861797 #> [6]  0.361721696 head(my_info_extractor$beta_x_covariates(model = fit_and_data)) #> [1] 4.056695 4.482596 5.284458 6.624113 3.801724 6.584892 my_simulator <- GOF_sim_wild_rademacher$new(   gof_model_info_extractor = my_info_extractor ) head(d) #>           x          y #> 1  8.124069 -0.9199426 #> 2  8.976991 -0.9666172 #> 3 10.582827 -1.0191812 #> 4 13.265662  0.3741709 #> 5  7.613455 -0.7480823 #> 6 13.187117  0.6588717 head(my_simulator$resample_y(model = fit_and_data)) #> [1] -0.6653077 -0.9808097 -1.0191812  0.3741709 -0.4783588  0.6588717 my_nls_trainer <- R6::R6Class(   classname = "GOF_nls_trainer",   inherit = GOF_model_trainer,   public = list(     refit = function(model, data) {       fit <- update(object = model$fit, data = data)       ret <- list(fit = fit, data = data)       return(ret)     })) my_trainer <- my_nls_trainer$new() new_data <- d new_data$y <- my_simulator$resample_y(model = fit_and_data) my_trainer$refit(model = fit_and_data, data = new_data)$fit #> Nonlinear regression model #>   model: y ~ sin(a * x) #>    data: data #>      a  #> 0.4997  #>  residual sum-of-squares: 7.871 #>  #> Number of iterations to convergence: 2  #> Achieved convergence tolerance: 1.49e-08 set.seed(1) mt <- GOF_model_test$new(   model = fit_and_data,   data = d,   nmb_boot_samples = 100,   y_name = "y",   Rn1_statistic = Rn1_CvM$new(),   gof_model_info_extractor = my_info_extractor,   gof_model_resample = GOF_model_resample$new(     gof_model_simulator = my_simulator,     gof_model_trainer = my_trainer   ) ) mt$get_pvalue() #> [1] 0.8

title: New-Models
text: negative binomial model generalized linear model. Furthermore, within R MASS::glm.nb returns object class glm package actually can process glm-classes. However, MASS::glm.nb seems bug prevents propoerly update/refit object via stats::update() function. briefly illustrate using artificial data set: Note fit-object shows call contained parameter init.theta obviously provided us. problem init.theta parameter used stats::update refitting resampled data. fitting resampled data fitting original data slightly different perspective fitting algorithm. circumvent problem can reimplement corresponding interface follows: way ensure original data set resampled data set fitted way. Now can create GOF-test-class using new refitting-class Lets compare result default GOF-test glm’s case p-values differ. However, different settings.
code: library(MASS) set.seed(1) X1 <- rnorm(100) X2 <- rnorm(100) d <- data.frame(   y = MASS::rnegbin(n = 100, mu = exp(0.2 + X1 * 0.2 + X2 * 0.6), theta = 2),   x1 = X1,   x2 = X2) fit <- MASS::glm.nb(y~x1+x2, data = d) fit #>  #> Call:  MASS::glm.nb(formula = y ~ x1 + x2, data = d, init.theta = 1.561918046,  #>     link = log) #>  #> Coefficients: #> (Intercept)           x1           x2   #>      0.1905       0.1532       0.7696   #>  #> Degrees of Freedom: 99 Total (i.e. Null);  97 Residual #> Null Deviance:       144.3  #> Residual Deviance: 102.4     AIC: 317.5 my_negbin_trainer <- R6::R6Class(   classname = "GOF_glmnb_trainer",   inherit = GOF_model_trainer,   public = list(     refit = function(model, data) {       MASS::glm.nb(formula = formula(model), data = data)     })) set.seed(1) mt <- GOF_model_test$new(   model = fit,   data = d,   nmb_boot_samples = 100,   y_name = "y",   Rn1_statistic = Rn1_CvM$new(),   gof_model_info_extractor = GOF_glm_info_extractor$new(),   gof_model_resample = GOF_model_resample$new(     gof_model_simulator = GOF_glm_sim_param$new(),     gof_model_trainer = my_negbin_trainer$new()   ) ) mt$get_pvalue() #> [1] 0.36 set.seed(1) mt2 <- GOF_model(   model = fit,   data = d,   nmb_boot_samples = 100,   simulator_type = "parametric",   y_name = "y",   Rn1_statistic = Rn1_CvM$new() ) #> Warning in GOF_model(model = fit, data = d, nmb_boot_samples = 100, #> simulator_type = "parametric", : The GOF-test requires to refit the model. #> Refitting MASS::glm.nb can be problematic, see vignette New-Models mt2$get_pvalue() #> [1] 0.36
